gloss: busy period; busy season; peak period

definitions.gloss: busy period; busy season; peak season
definitions.explanation: A time of year or period when work, business, or activity is particularly intense and demanding.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}は{多忙期|たぼうき}で{休|やす}めない。
examples.english: I can't take time off because the end of the year is a busy period.

examples.japanese: {多忙期|たぼうき}には{残業|ざんぎょう}が{増|ふ}える。
examples.english: During the busy period, overtime increases.

examples.japanese: {多忙期|たぼうき}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えるために、{臨時|りんじ}スタッフを{採用|さいよう}した。
examples.english: To get through the busy period, we hired temporary staff.

notes:
A compound of {多忙|たぼう} (very busy) and {期|き} (period, season). Describes a time when workload or business activity peaks. Common in workplace and business contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {多忙期|たぼうき}に{入|はい}る: to enter a busy period
- {多忙期|たぼうき}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}える: to get through a busy period
- {多忙期|たぼうき}と{閑散期|かんさんき}: busy period and slow period
- {年末|ねんまつ}の{多忙期|たぼうき}: the year-end busy period

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {繁忙期|はんぼうき}: busy season — essentially synonymous; {繁忙期|はんぼうき} is slightly more common in business and tourism contexts
- {閑散期|かんさんき}: slow period, off-season — the opposite of {多忙期|たぼうき}; when business or activity is at its lowest
- {ピーク: peak — a loanword often used to describe the busiest point within a busy period

NOTE:
Typical busy periods in Japan include {年末年始|ねんまつねんし} (year-end and New Year), {年度末|ねんどまつ} (end of fiscal year in March), and {決算期|けっさんき} (closing of accounts). In the travel industry, お{盆|ぼん} (mid-August) and ゴールデンウィーク (Golden Week in late April/early May) are major busy seasons.
